Freezing the repair cases is a specification act only: design changes cannot alter src/tests/pyproject, so this stage wrote no source, test, schema, fixture or packaging byte. The implementation stage must create each frozen identifier verbatim and must add the repair cases without removing, renaming or weakening any of the 139 inherited cases.

Planned unit-case identifiers are full pytest node identifiers of the form tests/thesis_lite/argus/<module>.py::test_<case>; they are module-level functions with no hyphen, so the trusted discovery normalization test_id.replace('-','_') is a no-op and each identifier appears verbatim in verbose pytest output.

The 33 new cases and 6 additive repair static checks are grounded in the terminal-review required fixes and the repaired detailed-design sections (4.4, 8.5, 11.1, 12.1, 12.2, 14.1); they specify bounded streaming I/O, pre-I/O confined regular-file checks, closed nested schemas and stable diagnostics, reader-assessed corrupt-evidence status, the actual serialized byte bound at every manifest publication, and deep admission snapshots with immutable returned views. No scientific protocol number, threshold, tolerance, deadline, repetition, seed or run identity is chosen, defaulted or narrowed anywhere in the specification.

Evidence reason codes (ARGUS2-REASON-*) remain manifest facts; the two new reader-assessed codes ARGUS2-REASON-CORRUPT-MANIFEST and ARGUS2-REASON-CORRUPT-EVENT are assigned only by the reader and are never written into a manifest by the writer.
The per-unit repair static checks are planned inputs to the ARGUS2-STATIC analysis owned by the verification-design stage; no static analysis is executed in this stage.

Distinct stage artifacts remain immutable and nonshared: the requirements, architecture and prior-stage records listed as inputs are byte-preserved, and later stages must regenerate their own records rather than overwrite this stage's artifacts.
